Financial limitations and COVID-19 disruptions compelled ANC to focus exclusively on the Tribal IRA Office (Figure 1), targeting a reduction in energy costs through high-impact retrofits, i.e., retrofits that could result in a quick return on investment without exceeding the available budget. This strategic pivot sought to maximize economic benefits and provide groundwork for future community- wide energy improvements. Figure 1: The Tribal Office building in Akiachak. Image by N. Overview Task 1: Project Kickoff In the first quarter of the project, ANC staff, NREL staff, and the energy auditor met virtually to review project goals and finalize planning documents. The Tribal IRA Office was benchmarked against a 2017 energy audit. The building’s annual energy usage was assessed in terms of energy use intensity (EUI) and fuel oil usage relative to cumulative base 65o heating degree days (HDDs) across the sample period to understand each building’s performance over time further and investigate potential energy anomalies. This project—originally intended to implement energy efficiency retrofits for five Akiachak buildings audited in 2017—faced significant delays because of the COVID-19 pandemic and workforce capacity issues. 1.1 Document the present conditions of the project buildings: The energy auditor (re)documented the current condition of the five buildings and noted some changes since the earlier energy audits. 1.2 Create a data management plan: Staff developed a data management plan detailing roles and responsibilities for the energy savings verification process. The plan outlined methods for data collection and secure storage throughout the project duration. 1.3 Create an outreach plan: Staff developed an outreach plan to inform and educate Tribal members about the project scope and the benefits of energy efficiency upgrades. 1.4 COVID mitigation plan: At the time of implementation, ANC no longer required this subtask. Task 2: Hire Retrofit Contractors Project staff developed detailed scopes of work for lighting and mechanical systems. Requests for Proposals (RFPs) were issued, and at least three bids were obtained for each category. Contractors were hired by the end of the third quarter of the project. After re-evaluating the scope of work in 2023, the focus was narrowed to the Tribal Office. ANC, in collaboration with an energy auditor, adjusted the project scope to fit a reduced budget, which included upgrades in HVAC (replacing thermostats and improving hydronic heating systems) and lighting (replacing with LED).
